burden_policy: NOT_COVERED: This passage explains the evidentiary significance attributed to the register entry but does not formulate a general burden-of-proof rule for statutory acquisition.
unimplemented: Independent authentication and admissibility assessment of the register.
Determination of the precise statutory mechanism through which ownership was acquired.
Assessment of the entry's probative weight against other evidence.

burden_policy: NOT_COVERED: The judgment identifies admissible evidence and records as necessary to establish ownership, possession and title, but does not provide a complete general allocation of evidentiary burdens for every competing title theory.
unimplemented: Combined evaluation of documentary evidence and testimony.
Independent determination of admissibility, authenticity, credibility and evidentiary weight.
Resolution of acquisition versus guardianship as the precise statutory mechanism.
Evaluation of the competing historical Wakf ownership case against the claimant's documentary evidence.
Independent determination of title under statutory provisions whose complete texts were not supplied.
A deterministic checker cannot execute the OPEN_TEXT ownership evaluation merely because the listed favorable propositions have been recorded.

burden_policy: SUPPORTED WITHIN THE STATED SCOPE: The judgment expressly places on the person claiming adverse possession the responsibility to clearly plead and establish all facts necessary for that claim. No broader burden rule is inferred.
unimplemented: Independent review of the original pleadings and evidence.
Assessment of whether differently expressed factual allegations could legally satisfy the required specificity.
Substantive evaluation of the complete adverse-possession standard.
Determination of an actual dispossession date or applicable limitation period from information not provided.

burden_policy: NOT_COVERED: The reported precedent establishes the substantive significance of disclaimer and hostile possession but does not supply a complete procedural burden allocation for proving renunciation in these appeals.
unimplemented: Determination of whether a legally effective renunciation of the original title basis occurred.
Determination of when any such renunciation occurred relative to the alleged hostile possession.
Semantic reconciliation of alternative pleadings under the particular procedural record.
Application of the complete reasoning of cited precedents without access to their independent judgments.

burden_policy: SUPPORTED: The party asserting adverse possession must clearly plead and prove every legally necessary fact supporting that claim. The judgment expressly assigns that obligation to the adverse-possession claimant, who seeks to defeat the true owner's rights. Any more detailed burden or evidentiary-presumption framework is NOT_COVERED.
unimplemented: Contextual legal evaluation of hostility, exclusivity, animus possidendi, continuity, publicity and extent of possession.
Identification of the relevant true owner and any wrongful dispossession.
Assessment of the actual date and duration of alleged adverse possession.
Identification and application of the governing statutory period to the particular property and circumstances.
Determination of whether the original-title theory was effectively renounced.
Assessment of whether the specific pleading and proof deficiencies are legally decisive in the particular record.
The OPEN_TEXT evaluation cannot be executed as a deterministic checklist of the listed adverse-possession factors.

burden_policy: NOT_COVERED: This rule concerns the logical independence of the original-title and adverse-possession grounds. It does not impose an additional burden of proof or allocate appellate burdens.
unimplemented: Execution of R2's underlying OPEN_TEXT evidentiary assessment.
Execution of R5's underlying OPEN_TEXT adverse-possession assessment.
Independent determination of all requirements for sustaining or dismissing the appeals.
Any broader rule concerning the effect of an unsuccessful alternative pleading on an appeal beyond the distinction demonstrated by the judgment.
